Re: reporting control/status responses for inband signaling?
quotation
I'll do my best to figure it out.

quotation
I should note here that the USRP doesn't care which application on the
host requests the different actions, which is probably why we have the
fixed channel of 0x1f. The USRP is simply the endpoint.

quotation
Looking at the payload of the control channel, any of the op codes
that write something and then have the USRP reply back seem to have an
RID within them to determine where to send things back.

This is probably what should be inserted/stripped by the usrp_server
to figure out which application receives the reply.

I can see this working where the Application requests something (ping
perhaps?) and sends the ping request to the usrp_server. The
usrp_server constructs the packet with the next available RID
(probably just some incremental counter mod 64, or if you don't expect
one application to have multiple outstanding commands, just a unique
number for each application which is reused - just ideas and you know
this more than I would). After the USRP then processes the command
and sends the reply back, the usrp_server will read the RID field of
the received packet and forward the packet (minus the RID) back to the
Application.

I could be missing it just as much as you did, but what do you think about that?

closing

Ok, it's time for the monday mini-freeze status again.

Nothing has changed since then, sadly, i have sent a follow up to the
bug report, but i doubt it will help.

Our packages are still, as far i can see, olden up by postgresql and
libvorbis. I believe that the postgresql situation will be fixed nextly,
as the maintainer is actively working on it, still there may be
dependency on perl 5.8 and such, which may block it even if it becomes a
valid candidate.

The libvorbis is more murky, i attach here a partial dependency check,
but it is is not complete and tied in with many really broken packages,
including the new KDE, so i have no hope for a quick solution.

I only see 4 solutions for us going forward :

o We stop the mini-freeze and don't care about testing anymore.

o I upload my ocaml-3.06 package, which altough it is not yet the real
one i wanted, will enter testing because nothing is holding it, and
with it will go most of the libraries and executable packages.

o I work more on the ocaml-3.06 package, and do true binary separation
and parallel installation. I don't really have time for it though.

o You and Jerome rebuild ocamlsdl and libpgsql with a system
consisting of testing + ocaml 3.06 packages. This gets uploaded to
unstable (little breakage of sid maybe, but it should not be long)
log

Re: XP weaknesses --- Fixed Price
I think I see where the difference is, Dominic, let's see if I can capture
it...
It looks to me as that you are thinking:
(A) IF we're using XP, THEN it fits the fixed price-scene scene
(which it doesn't, using your terms - large chunks of XP don't get exercised)
but Ron and I are thinking:
(B) IF we're in the fixed-price scene THEN XP (or what large chunks of
it we can still use) works better that the alternatives.

So we're okay with ignoring certain availabilities that XP otherwise might
give us
(like adding and replacing cards across iterations) in order to have access
to
other availabilities that XP gives us (like PP and refactoring and TDD and
short iterations and ...)

while it looks as though you are so unhappy with what gets cut out of XP
that you wouldn't even call it XP any more. ... Trying that on for size for
a minute, I'm guessing that in the fixed-price situation you'd still aim
for short iterations, access to customer, PP, TDD, DTSTTCPW, refactoring,
colocation? You'd still do the parts of XP that fit, even though you might
have to call it WP instead.

p.s. thanks for registering that you disagree about requirements
gathering being outside XP. Until you wrote that I didn't notice.
I thought this group was in general agreement with Ron about
requirements gathering being outside XP.

closing

quotation

Remote security
The machine I use day to day is the machine I sure as the server for unison.

I have a laptop that syncs with it
A linux media centre (MythTV) that I plan to sync with it as soon as I
get the right unison version on there
and a machine in an office in London that I only go to once per month or so.

Currently, to sync the London machine, I log into it using TightVNC over
Hamachi (can't get ssh to work in the direction from my home machine to
the office so I use hamachi) then run unison from there.

Before yesterday, I would manually run Putty every time I wanted to
sync, which was a pain, but as least meant that an ssh connection from
the office machine to my machine was only temporary.

Now, I've set up Pageant so that I don't have to use putty all the time
(although that's not cured a problem I was having so not sure how great
a solution it is) which is handy. The down side is that I'm feeling
insecure about a constant ssh tunnel from a location I can't monitor to
my main machine.

Is there anything I can do to make this more secure?
Can I somehow make unison the only app that it's possible to run over
ssh/pageant?

I can't even think of other possibilities, but looking forward to
hearing any thoughts.

closing
